A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, title, theoretical framework, and original experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable; v3 retains Appendices A–E and adds F–G.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original ProsQA graph-reachability experiments, including answer accuracies, attention-logit trajectories, and candidate-lift attention maps.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds architectural and optimization ablations, four-layer representation analyses, and answer-prediction accuracy dynamics in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The continuous-thought procedure, curriculum, COCONUT and COCONUT-BFS objectives, and prediction mechanism are unchanged. The deeper, wider, and untied models in Appendix F are additional configurations evaluated under the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate graph reachability on the same ProsQA subset with permuted vertex indices. Table 3 retains the same dataset statistics. Appendix F varies models and optimization without adding a dataset, task, or distinct input scenario.

E2.justification: Both retain the comparison with the frontier-only experimental COCONUT-BFS variant defined in Equation 19 and evaluated in Appendix E.2. The new experiments are within-method ablations; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds controlled evaluations across depth, attention-head count, width, learning rate, and weight tying, plus extended first-stage budgets of 300 and 400 epochs. It also introduces layer-wise representation measurements for a four-layer model. These substantially expand the evaluated settings while the original Section 5 protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 retains the original logit dynamics and alternative candidate-lift analyses, then adds substantial supplementary investigation: architectural and optimization sensitivity in Table 4, copying and superposition across four layers in Figures 7–8, and accuracy dynamics alongside prediction signals in Figure 9.

E5.justification: The qualitative reference to different random seeds in Section 5.2 is retained. The added table and plots introduce no run counts, explicit seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original COCONUT accuracy of 96.2% and COCONUT-BFS accuracy of 99.0% remain. New results include 67.4% for twelve layers under default settings and 99.6% with learning rate 5×10^-5 and 400 first-stage epochs, alongside four-layer mechanism and accuracy-dynamics findings. Table 4's new default accuracy of 98.8% is unexplained relative to the retained 96.2%, so it cannot establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical definitions, equations, theorem statements, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–D are retained. Section 2.1 illustrates the existing index-matching and frontier-expansion mechanism without introducing new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, central introduction claims, and conclusion retain the same contribution: explaining superposition through bounded index-matching logits and analyzing thought generation and answer prediction. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds interpretations of optimization sensitivity and four-layer representations, arguing that superposition appears from the second layer onward. It also qualifies the single-hyperparameter ablations by acknowledging coupled effects and leaving comprehensive interaction studies open. Existing theory–experiment qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F documents exact sweep configurations, the rule that other settings remain fixed, and extended training schedules used in additional experiments. Existing optimizer, batch-size, curriculum, and dataset details are retained, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Huang et al. (2025b) on CoT length generalization, Lin et al. (2025) on identity bridges, and Ma et al. (2026) on the reversal curse. The paper's positioning as a training-dynamics explanation following Hao et al. and Zhu et al. remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds an intuitive introductory subsection on local search and index-matching logits, Appendix F, and an LLM writing-use disclosure in Appendix G. Publication headers and some related-work prose are updated, while the existing narrative, technical sections, and proofs remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially through the two-part conceptual Figure 2, ablation Table 4, four-layer attention and representation Figures 7–8, and Figure 9's accuracy overlay on the retained prediction-signal curves. Original figures remain, with corresponding renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: The intuitive explanation and diagrams improve accessibility, while Appendix F provides useful evidence about optimization sensitivity and mechanisms beyond two-layer models. These strengthen the paper without changing its central theory. The unexplained difference between Table 4's 98.8% default accuracy and Section 5's retained 96.2% limits confidence in the added comparisons, making the overall improvement modest.
